subject: Clarify: isolation runbook, keystore residency & ops handoff
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Allegra Singh <allegra@medsyn.com>, Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@medsyn.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-21T14:08:00Z
Subject: Post-call: isolation expectations & next steps

Thanks for the call earlier today — quick recap and the two clarifying questions we promised to follow up on. Great discussion; sounds like Medsyn is prioritizing clear custody controls for PHI in the POC.

Recap (short):
- Primary ask: separation of customer data from other tenants; strict control-plane separation for auditability.
- Preference: Private VPC with customer KMS, but open to Dedicated if we can demonstrate identical custody guarantees.
- Next milestone: ops workshop to validate keystore residency and audit evidence.

Two clarifying questions (please reply inline):
1) When you say "keystore must be in our control" — do you require Redwood to integrate with your KMS (customer-managed CMK in your AWS account) for all encryption-at-rest operations, or is BYOK via wrapped keys acceptable?
2) For the data-plane: is physical host exclusivity required (no co-tenancy on the same GPU hosts), or is logical isolation within dedicated tenancy acceptable?

Attached: draft runbook stub we promised (isolation_runbook_v1.pdf) and a simple keystore mapping CSV. We'll use these as the basis for the ops workshop.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm answers to the two questions above by EOD Wed (6/25).
- Schedule a 60-min ops workshop (Connor + our infra ops) next week to validate architecture and evidence.
- We'll put together a short comparison doc showing equivalence paths: Private VPC vs Dedicated with strict tenancy controls.

Thanks — happy to adjust cadence.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments referenced: isolation_runbook_v1.pdf (pdf), keystore_map.csv (csv)

From: Allegra Singh <allegra@medsyn.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@medsyn.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-21T18:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: isolation expectations & next steps

Thanks Ben — good summary. Inline answers below.

1) KMS / keystore residency:
- We require customer-managed keys that meet FIPS 140-2 level 3 controls. Ideally the CMK lives in our AWS account and Redwood calls it via a cross-account KMS grant.
- If cross-account CMK is not feasible, we can accept wrapped keys (BYOK) only if the unwrapping key never leaves our HSM and you provide documented proof of the unwrapping procedure during the POC.

2) Data-plane isolation:
- We want exclusivity at the tenant level; that can be satisfied by Private VPC (preferred) where the data-plane lives in our subnet and its traffic never traverses shared host network overlays.
- Dedicated tenancy may work only if you guarantee no shared GPU hosts (physical host tenancy), enforce strict network egress restrictions, and provide evidence (host inventory + placement logs) for the POC.

Evidence and compliance asks for POC:
- KMS configuration guide and cross-account grant example.
- Host placement proof and audit logs showing no co-tenancy.
- Retention window & access logging for control plane actions (who accessed keys, when).

We'll loop in our security operations to the ops workshop. Attaching Medsyn security checklist for your reference.

Allegra
Head of Cloud Security
Medsyn Health
---
Attachments referenced: Medsyn_Security_Checklist_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Allegra Singh <allegra@medsyn.com>, Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@medsyn.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-22T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: isolation expectations & next steps

Allegra — thanks for the clear answers, and thanks for sharing the checklist. Quick responses and what we'll bring to the ops workshop.

KMS approach (what we can offer):
- Cross-account KMS grant into your AWS account: Redwood can call a CMK that resides in Medsyn's account. We use an IAM role + KMS Grant for the POC.
- BYOK/wrapped keys: supported as an alternate path; we'll document the key-unwrapping flow and provide a reviewed runbook.

Data-plane tenancy (options):
- Private VPC: we can deploy the inference nodes into your VPC via our Private deployment model. Data-plane traffic will be confined to your VPC subnets and transit via your NAT/SG rules.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed tenancy): we can provision dedicated GPU pools with strict placement controls. For the POC we'll produce host placement manifests and periodic placement logs to show there is no GPU co-tenancy.

What Connor will validate in the ops workshop:
- Exact steps for configuring cross-account KMS grants and sample IAM policies.
- Method to export host placement evidence and the cadence of those exports during the POC.
- Control-plane access logging retention settings and where logs are stored for audit.

Deliverables before the call:
- Draft ops checklist (attached: isolation_runbook_v1.pdf) with named owners.
- Short comparison table showing tradeoffs: Private VPC vs Dedicated (we'll circulate by tomorrow).

If that aligns, Connor and I will propose two 60-min windows for the ops workshop.

Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
